definitions.explanation: Describes a firm, unwavering attitude or manner, especially when facing opposition or difficult situations. Implies moral courage and steadfast determination.

examples.japanese: {毅然|きぜん}とした{態度|たいど}
{彼女|かのじょ}は{不正|ふせい}に{対|たい}して{毅然|きぜん}と{立|た}ち{向|む}かった。
examples.english: She stood up resolutely against the injustice.

examples.japanese: {脅|おど}しにも{屈|くっ}せず、{毅然|きぜん}とした{姿勢|しせい}で{交渉|こうしょう}に{臨|のぞ}んだ。
examples.english: Unfazed by threats, he approached the negotiations with a firm stance.

notes:
ADJECTIVE TYPE: Na-adjective. Almost always used adverbially as {毅然|きぜん}と or attributively as {毅然|きぜん}とした.

ADVERBIAL FORM: {毅然|きぜん}と (resolutely, firmly)

NUANCE: {毅然|きぜん} conveys moral strength and the courage to stand firm on principles. It suggests dignified determination, not just stubbornness.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {毅然|きぜん}とした{態度|たいど} (firm attitude)
- {毅然|きぜん}と{断|ことわ}る (to refuse firmly)
- {毅然|きぜん}と{立|た}ち{向|む}かう (to stand up resolutely)
- {毅然|きぜん}とした{姿勢|しせい} (unwavering stance)

RELATED WORDS:
- {断固|だんこ} (resolutely, firmly)
- {泰然|たいぜん} (calm, unperturbed)
- {凛|りん}とした (dignified, resolute)
